written_by: hand, from the RTL and the property text; never from sby output
step_rule: A check inside always @(posedge clk) samples the values of step k on the edge into step k+1, so sby reports it at step k+1. Step 0 is the initial state; initial assume (rst) holds rst high at step 0.
timeline: Step 0 reset. Step 1: req=0, start may rise. Step 2: req=1, cnt=0. Normal DELAY=2: step 3 cnt=1, step 4 ack=1 and req=0. f_wait counts steps with req high and no ack: 1 at step 3, 2 at step 4, then 0.

prove.why: All three assertions are invariants of the normal design: ack is a one-cycle pulse (ack forces req low on the same edge, so ack cannot be set again on the next one), ack is only set from a cycle with req high, and req stays high for exactly two cycles before ack, so f_wait never exceeds 2. Each one is also k-inductive within depth 12.

prove_bug.why: BUG_ACK_LATE sets DELAY=4, so req stays high from step 2 to step 5 with no ack. f_wait is 1, 2, 3 at steps 3, 4, 5. The f_wait <= 2 check sees 3 on the edge out of step 5 and fails at step 6. The other two assertions still hold: the late ack is still a one-cycle pulse that follows a cycle with req high.

cover.why: The single cover (f_past_valid && !rst && ack) is first true at step 4, the first step with ack high, so it is reached at step 5.
